sources.name: OGC API - Processes - Part 1: Core
sources.role: process description, input/output, execution request, job status and result retrieval contract
verified_facts: The standard exposes process metadata and detailed descriptions of process inputs and outputs.
An HTTP POST to a process execution endpoint creates a job and passes inputs and requested outputs in a JSON execute request.
The job status resource is identified through the Location header, and results or exceptions are retrieved after success or failure.
semantic_limits: A process description does not prove that the deployed algorithm, parameters or source data match the parcel-height method.
A successful job state does not independently prove complete source-byte consumption, exact parcel containment or numeric accuracy.
A returned output remains support-only until source digest, process version, CRS, vertical datum, units and execution provenance are bound.

sources.name: OGC API - Environmental Data Retrieval Standard 1.1
sources.role: position, area, cube, trajectory and corridor query selection and response contract
verified_facts: EDR collection metadata may advertise position, radius, area, cube, trajectory and corridor query types.
Valid position queries combine coordinates with optional time, parameter-name, vertical level, CRS and output-format selectors and return matching information.
Cube, trajectory and corridor conformance tests require valid spatial parameters and verify that only information matching selection criteria is returned.
semantic_limits: An EDR response is a selected subset and must not be treated as the complete underlying environmental source.
A z or vertical-level selector does not by itself identify EPSG:5701, Ordnance Datum Newlyn or the height reference used by a value.
HTTP 200 and schema conformance do not establish exact HMLR parcel geometry, source authority or measurement accuracy.

sources.name: OGC API - Moving Features - Part 1: Core
sources.role: moving-feature identity, temporal geometry, trajectory query, filtering and update contract
verified_facts: The standard defines RESTful interfaces and data formats for querying and updating moving-feature data.
It supports discovery and retrieval of moving features and temporal characteristics such as positions or velocity over time intervals.
Moving-feature item responses may be limited by bounding box, datetime, limit and sub-trajectory parameters.
semantic_limits: A temporal position or trajectory is not a cadastral parcel boundary and must not be substituted for exact HMLR geometry.
A filtered sub-trajectory is not a complete observation history or a static terrain surface.
Velocity, aggregation or temporal-geometry conformance does not provide a parcel maximum-minus-minimum elevation result.

sources.name: OGC API - Discrete Global Grid Systems - Part 1: Core
sources.role: DGGRS zone, resolution level, zone geometry, centroid and data representation contract
verified_facts: The standard provides API building blocks for retrieving data organized by a discrete global grid reference system.
Representations may use zone centroids, zone regions or vectorized geometries depending on the requested geometry mode.
A response CRS may follow the DGGRS or underlying geographic CRS, and clients may request supported geometry representations.
semantic_limits: A DGGS zone identifier or hierarchy level is not an exact HMLR parcel polygon or a DEM native-resolution statement.
A zone centroid is a representative point and must not be treated as the parcel boundary or the location of an elevation extremum.
An aggregated cell value or vectorized zone value is not a point measurement and cannot create a parcel height-difference business row.
